name: UT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price McAdams at 94-95% to win
McAdams holds a massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage
No general-election polls, so fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The fundamentals point clearly to the Democrat: the redrawn UT-01 carries a D+12 partisan lean, Ben McAdams has raised over $2.2 million with $2.7 million in outside support while Riley Owen has raised under $150,000, and both Kalshi and Polymarket price a Democratic win around 94-95%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-implied margin of roughly 20 points.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Owen within single digits, or a late surge of Republican outside spending, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's first district is open after redistricting, and the new lines carry a Democratic-leaning partisan edge of about 12 points. Ben McAdams enters as the clear financial favorite, having raised $2.3 million and benefiting from $2.7 million in outside support, while Republican Riley Owen has raised only about $133,000 and reported under $10,000 on hand. Independent and Libertarian candidates also appear on the ballot but lack resources.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and markets. Both Kalshi and Polymarket price a Democratic win at roughly 94-95 percent. The expected margin is about 20 points, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling, but the district's lean and the money gap make an upset unlikely.
